findings.disposition: the top-level 6.01(a) prohibition rules carry entityScope ["BORROWER"] while their own provenance excerpt binds 'the Borrowers ... and ... any of their Restricted Subsidiaries'; the Permitted Ratio Debt permissions carry ["BORROWER"] while the source lets 'any of their Restricted Subsidiaries' incur. entityScope is an authoritative field (the real EntityClassTag enum, IR types.ts). A consumer reading it would conclude the prohibition binds only the Borrower (permissive-direction error) and that a Restricted Subsidiary cannot rely on the ratio permission (restrictive-direction error). The prohibition rules are PARTIAL and two ratio rules are COMPLETE, but no sufficiency reason, condition or limitation mentions scope, so the partiality does not prevent reliance on the wrong scope. Not explicitly limited anywhere (§11: not inferable from the top-level REVIEW_REQUIRED). The frozen run had entityScope empty everywhere (unspecified); the v5 prompt + fallback made the field populated and this run populated it under-inclusively.

findings.disposition: frozen source (region offset 16856): 'provided that: (a) ...; (b) ...; (c) (X) ... or (Y) ...; or (d) such Indebtedness constitutes Acquired Indebtedness ...; (e) solely to the extent not permitted to be incurred in reliance on clauses (a) through (d) above ...'. The list is joined by semicolons with a single 'or' before (d) and (e) is a residual over '(a) through (d)': the ordinary drafting reading is DISJUNCTIVE - any one of (a), (b), (c) or (d) qualifies the acquisition debt. The verifier's cumulative reading ((a) AND (b) AND ((c) OR (d))) is not supported by the punctuation and would make Acquired Indebtedness (d) subject to three ratio tests, which the residual (e) drafting contradicts. Under the disjunctive reading the IR's (c)/(d)/(e) structure is faithful, but the IR fuses (a) and (b) into ONE rule gated by AND(OR(a-tests), OR(b-tests)) - an OVER-RESTRICTIVE grouping (it denies debt that satisfies only (a) or only (b)). That is a representation inaccuracy in the conservative direction: it cannot lead a consumer to believe something is permitted that the source prohibits. The (14) family is also flagged by Pass C (its (x)/(y) subject items are MISSING) so the unit is REVIEW_REQUIRED. Recorded as a bounded, conservative grouping error; the interpretive disagreement is disclosed.
